dedupe_keys.name: towards non contact pollution monitoring in sewers with hyperspectral imaging

description: Pierre Lechevallier and colleagues at Eawag describe a non-contact model for estimating raw-wastewater pollution from hyperspectral images. Automated pixel selection and partial-least-squares regression predict seven variables, including chemical oxygen demand, turbidity, dissolved organic compounds, ammonium, nitrogen, phosphate and sulphates. The laboratory evaluation uses 144 samples of raw/diluted wastewater and synthetic turbidity solutions. The native description states that pixel and wavelength selection affect prediction performance. Zenodo supplies the article freely under CC BY 4.0; this is the publication licence, not a verified software licence. Coverage is the controlled wastewater experiment; exact dates and independent field validation are unspecified. Related conference deposits describe the same method and are grouped as support. A limitation is that source code, image data and model coefficients were not obtained, and reported precision was not independently checked.
